title: FCC deepfake election robocall enforcement
system_purpose: AI voice cloning and caller-ID spoofing used to distribute an election message
decision_impact: Whether potential voters receive and may act on a purported official voting instruction
affected_groups: Potential voters; people impersonated by synthetic media; election administrators; the public
verified_facts: The FCC adopted a $6 million fine against political consultant Steve Kramer for illegal spoofed robocalls that used an AI-generated clone of President Biden's voice and told potential New Hampshire primary voters not to vote.
reported_harm: The FCC says the calls spread election misinformation. The enforcement record confirms the regulator's action, but it does not measure how many recipients changed voting behavior.
quantitative_evidence: The calls occurred before the New Hampshire primary; the FCC adopted the $6 million fine on 2024-09-26. This pack does not infer a recipient denominator or voter-behavior effect.
limitations: This was U.S. voice-based election interference rather than a Vietnamese retrieval-grounded text assistant, so it supports a narrow synthetic-claim and provenance control rather than a claim of equivalent impact.

title: UK ICO political-data analytics investigation
system_purpose: Political campaign data analytics and targeting
decision_impact: Use of personal data to target political communications
affected_groups: Voters; social-media users; people whose political interests may be inferred
verified_facts: The UK ICO reported an investigation into political data analytics involving political parties, platforms, data brokers, and analytics firms, and documented regulatory action arising from it.
reported_harm: Opaque collection, matching, and use of political or social data can threaten privacy, autonomy, and trust in democratic communication. The report is not a causal estimate of influence on any individual voter.
quantitative_evidence: The report documents an investigation and regulatory action, but it does not provide a single product-comparable causal rate of voter influence; no such rate is claimed in this pack.
limitations: The historical UK investigation does not determine behavior or legal duties for a fixed-corpus Vietnamese research prototype that prohibits profiling and targeting.

title: Political fact-checking LLM evaluation with curated context
system_purpose: LLMs classify political claims with and without reasoning, web search, and a curated retrieval-augmented evidence set
decision_impact: Whether a user receives a reliable political-claim characterization and relevant evidence
affected_groups: Readers relying on civic information; people discussed in claims; fact-checkers and publishers whose evidence is represented
verified_facts: An ACL 2026 evaluation tested 15 recent LLMs on more than 6,000 PolitiFact claims. It found standard models performed poorly, web search made only moderate gains, and curated retrieval context improved macro-F1 by 233% on average across model variants.
reported_harm: This is a controlled evaluation rather than a deployed incident. It establishes a foreseeable hazard: a civic assistant can mischaracterize a political claim when retrieval is weak, irrelevant, or insufficient, even if it shows a citation.
quantitative_evidence: The evaluation covers 15 LLMs and more than 6,000 claims; curated context improved macro-F1 by 233% on average. It does not measure Vietnamese-language performance, breaking-news performance, beliefs, or sharing.
limitations: The benchmark is principally based on U.S. PolitiFact data and cannot establish CivicBrief's performance; it supports a testable curated-corpus, claim-to-evidence, and abstention requirement.
